facts.big: I'd like to make an appointment
facts.label: Marcar uma consulta
facts.sub: Ao telefone, diga que quer marcar, dê seu nome, soletre o sobrenome e escolha dia e hora.

facts.label: Ligar antes
facts.sub: Nos EUA, a maioria dos consultórios trabalha com hora marcada. Ligue ou use o site, diga o motivo e escolha o horário. Em caso urgente, existem clínicas de pronto atendimento, com atendimento sem marcar.

facts.label: Documento e seguro
facts.sub: Na primeira consulta, costumam pedir documento com foto e cartão do seguro-saúde. Leve os dois, e pergunte na hora de marcar: “What should I bring?” Assim você evita problemas na recepção.

items.why: Most offices work by appointment, except urgent care places.

items.s: The office may ask you to spell your last name.
items.why: Spelling letter by letter avoids mistakes.

items.s: You never need to show an ID or insurance card.

pages.title: My first call to the doctor’s office · 1/3
paragraphs: Last week I needed to see a doctor in **Orlando**. I was nervous, because I had to make a phone call in English. I took a pen, a paper and my **insurance** card.
A man answered: “Good morning, **Dr. Rivera’s office**.” I said, “Hi. **I’d like to make an appointment**.” He said, “Sure. **What’s your name?**” I said, “It’s Alex Silva.”

pages.title: My first call to the doctor’s office · 2/3
paragraphs: Then he asked, “**How do you spell your last name?**” I said slowly, “**S-I-L-V-A**.” He repeated it. I was happy because he understood me.

He asked, “**When can you come?**” I said, “**Do you have time on Tuesday?**” He answered, “We have **ten o’clock** or **two o’clock**.” I like to go **early**, so I said, “Ten o’clock **works for me**.”
